overview: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America. Its capital and largest city is Managua. Nicaragua became independent from Spain in 1821. Its poet Rubén Darío is one of the most celebrated writers in the Spanish language.

geography.text: Nicaragua has two huge lakes: Lake Nicaragua, the largest lake in Central America, and Lake Managua. A line of volcanoes runs along the Pacific side of the country, where most people live. The Caribbean side, known as the Mosquito Coast, is wetter, with rainforest and far fewer people.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot and tropical, wetter on the Caribbean side.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Freshwater sharks in Lake Nicaragua and sea turtles that nest in huge numbers.

history.text: Spain colonised Nicaragua's Pacific side in the 1500s, while Britain held influence on the Caribbean coast. After independence in 1821, the American adventurer William Walker briefly made himself president in the 1850s. The Somoza family ruled as dictators from the 1930s until the Sandinista revolution of 1979, which was followed by the Contra war.

events.title: Granada founded
events.text: Spanish settlers found the city of Granada.

events.title: William Walker
events.text: An American adventurer seizes power before being driven out.

events.title: Elections end the war
events.text: Elections bring the Contra war to an end.

government.text: Nicaragua is officially a presidential republic, but President Daniel Ortega and his wife, Rosario Murillo, now share power as 'co-presidents' after constitutional changes in 2025. Opposition leaders have been jailed or exiled, and many independent organisations have been closed. International observers did not consider recent elections free or fair.

economy.text: Nicaragua is one of the poorest countries in the Americas. It exports gold, coffee, beef, sugar and clothing. Money sent home by Nicaraguans abroad is a large part of the economy.

culture.text: Nicaragua is known as the land of lakes and volcanoes. Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America and has freshwater sharks. The poet Rubén Darío, who started the modernismo movement in Spanish literature, is a national hero.

items.title: Lake Nicaragua
items.text: Home to more than 300 small islands.

items.title: El Güegüense
items.text: A satirical folk play listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Gallo pinto, rice and beans, and nacatamal, a large tamale wrapped in banana leaf.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Poetry is hugely popular; Granada hosts an international poetry festival.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: La Purísima, on 7 December, sees people go door to door singing for the Virgin Mary.

sport.text: Unlike most of Central America, Nicaragua's favourite sport is baseball, introduced by Americans in the 1800s. Boxing has also produced world champions, including Alexis Argüello and Román 'Chocolatito' González.

items.title: Alexis Argüello
items.text: World boxing champion in three weight classes.

items.title: Dennis Martínez
items.text: Pitched a perfect game in Major League Baseball in 1991.

didYouKnow: Lake Nicaragua is home to bull sharks that swim up the river from the Caribbean.
Nicaragua is sometimes called the 'land of lakes and volcanoes'.

keyPeople.name: Román González
keyPeople.text: World champion in four weight divisions.
